name: Credential Technology Assessment
hypothesis: Static, unauthenticated credential identifiers may permit credential replay or cloning where the access-control architecture does not provide cryptographic mutual authentication.
assessment_condition: Does the electronic credential broadcast a static unencrypted identifier (such as 125 kHz Prox or unauthenticated CSN) without cryptographic challenge-response validation?

steps: Hold sample authorized credential in proximity to the test reader.
Identify operating carrier frequency (125 kHz Low Frequency vs. 13.56 MHz High Frequency).

Identify observable credential technology and determine whether the credential exposes a static identifier. Reader-side cryptographic enforcement requires configuration evidence or authorized administrative verification.

evidence_requirements.validation_criteria: Documented carrier frequency and whether credential protocol implements cryptographic challenge-response authentication. Reader-side SAM configuration verified via administrative evidence.

result_model.hardened_criteria: Credential implements mutual cryptographic authentication (AES-128 / DESFire EV2/EV3 / Seos / PIV smartcard).
result_model.deficient_criteria: Credential relies on unencrypted 125 kHz Prox (HID Prox, EM4100) or static 13.56 MHz CSN without mutual authentication.
result_model.condition_requires_validation_criteria: High-frequency smartcard observed; reader-side SAM cryptographic validation requires administrative policy audit.

can_establish: Operating carrier frequency (LF 125 kHz vs. HF 13.56 MHz).
Exposure of static unencrypted credential identifiers on tested badge.
cannot_establish: Reader-side cryptographic key enforcement or SAM validation without administrative configuration evidence.
Whether secondary compensating factors (such as biometric verification or PACs duress monitoring) are enforced at readers.

mitigation_action: Upgrade credential stock to ISO/IEC 14443-4 smartcards with AES-128 mutual authentication (DESFire EV3 / Seos) and activate SAM keys on access readers.

Guidelines for the Use of PIV Credentials in Facility Access

name: Door & Latch Protection Assessment
hypothesis: Door and frame geometry may permit mechanical manipulation of the latch bolt assembly where protective physical shielding is absent and strike clearances exceed engineering tolerances.
assessment_condition: Does the outward-opening door assembly exhibit strike margin clearance exceeding 3.2mm (1/8 in.) with direct line-of-sight to the latch bolt and zero overlapping protective steel astragal guard, where applicable standards or specifications mandate tight margins or shielding?

steps: Inspect door swing direction (inward vs. outward opening).
Measure frame strike gap at latch level using feeler gauge.
Where the assessed opening is within the applicable NFPA 80 or ANSI/SDI scope, compare measured strike clearance against applicable assembly requirements.
Check for presence and full coverage of continuous stainless steel security astragal plate.

acceptable_formats: Photo of frame margin with gauge
evidence_requirements.validation_criteria: Where the assessed opening is within the applicable NFPA 80 scope, compare measured clearance against the applicable edition and assembly requirements.

result_model.hardened_criteria: Outward door fitted with continuous full-height steel astragal overlapping jamb; latch bolt fully shielded from direct mechanical access.
result_model.deficient_criteria: Exposed latch bolt with perimeter strike gap exceeding applicable specification (e.g. 3.2mm / 1/8 in.) and no exterior astragal plate.
result_model.condition_requires_validation_criteria: Perimeter gap exceeds 3.2mm on non-rated assembly where deadlocking auxiliary latch engagement requires physical verification.

can_establish: Exact perimeter gap measurements against fire and building standards.
Presence and structural alignment of protective astragal shielding.
cannot_establish: Internal lock cylinder integrity or mechanical deadbolt throw status without operational key/credential testing.

mitigation_action: Install full-height continuous stainless steel security astragal plate overlapping the door frame stop on the exterior approach side.

technical_references.title: Standard for Fire Doors and Other Opening Protectives
Specifications for Standard Steel Doors and Frames

name: REX Sensor Placement Assessment
hypothesis: Interior Request-to-Exit (REX) motion detectors whose detection cones extend to perimeter door margins may be susceptible to non-contact activation through door seams if directional shielding is absent.
assessment_condition: Is the interior Request-to-Exit (REX) passive infrared (PIR) sensor optical field or lens visible from the exterior through transom, jamb, or threshold margins without a directional deflector hood?

steps: Examine perimeter threshold, transom, and meeting stile gaps from the exterior side of the portal.
Determine if interior REX PIR sensor body or optical lens is within direct line-of-sight.
Verify presence of a directional deflector collar, shroud, or physical sensor hood.

acceptable_formats: Photo of interior transom from exterior gap
evidence_requirements.validation_criteria: Documented sensor presence, mounting angle, and shroud installation status.

result_model.hardened_criteria: REX sensor fitted with directional deflector hood restricting detection field strictly to the interior egress path; perimeter brush sweep or astragal installed.
result_model.deficient_criteria: Unshielded wide-angle PIR sensor lens directly visible through perimeter door seams where installation specifications explicitly mandate directional shrouding.
result_model.condition_requires_validation_criteria: Unshielded wide-angle PIR sensor body or lens visible through perimeter door gaps without a deflector hood; potential exterior trigger exposure requiring controlled validation or engineering review.

can_establish: Optical line-of-sight to the interior sensor lens from the exterior perimeter.
Presence of mechanical deflector hoods or perimeter brush sweeps.
cannot_establish: Actual sensor sensitivity threshold setting, PIR pulse count configuration, or whether environmental triggers can reliably trip the relay.

mitigation_action: Mount a directional metal deflector hood over the interior REX PIR sensor and install perimeter brush sweeps on door gaps.

technical_references.title: Life Safety Code - Sensor Release of Electrically Locked Egress Doors
Standard for Access Control System Units

name: Exposed Physical Network Interface Assessment
hypothesis: Publicly accessible network jacks that maintain an active physical link may provide unauthorized network connectivity if administrative port shutdown, 802.1X, or MAC-based quarantine is misconfigured.
assessment_condition: Does a publicly accessible RJ-45 Ethernet wall drop in an unmonitored or common area broadcast an active physical Layer 1 carrier signal upon non-intrusive connection?

tools_required: Passive LED Ethernet link state tester (zero-packet transmit)
steps: Connect passive LED link tester to the exposed common area RJ-45 wall drop.
Observe status indicator LEDs for Layer 1 electrical carrier detection (10/100/1000 Mbps).
Verify whether port is administratively shut down or disconnected at the patch panel.

acceptable_formats: LED carrier indicator status (Illuminated vs. Unilluminated)
Port label and physical location identifier
evidence_requirements.validation_criteria: Documented link carrier state without transmitting IP packets or conducting network probing.

result_model.hardened_criteria: Zero Layer 1 link state (port administratively shut down or unpatched at switch level) OR documented 802.1X port-security policy confirmed enforced.
result_model.deficient_criteria: Active Layer 1 link carrier continuously illuminated on unmonitored common-area drop with verified absence of 802.1X or administrative port shutdown policy.
result_model.condition_requires_validation_criteria: Active Layer 1 link carrier observed on unmonitored drop; network access control (802.1X), VLAN isolation, and MAC quarantine status require administrative verification.

can_establish: Physical Layer 1 carrier signaling and electrical continuity.
Whether port is administratively shut down at the hardware layer.
cannot_establish: Whether IEEE 802.1X network access control (NAC) is enforced upon frame transmission.
VLAN segmentation, DHCP address assignment, or lateral IP connectivity.

mitigation_action: Administratively shut down unused common area switch ports at the patch panel or configure strict IEEE 802.1X port authentication.
